findings.title: Intrinsic due right and normative comparison
findings.finding: Actual desire is not a condition of every obligation. Real benefaction, excellence and rightful relation can warrant nonpunitive acknowledgment, love and obedience. This positive case does not by itself establish that every categorical reason requires God. James distinguishes finite ethical reality without God from a final encompassing divine standard; Railtonian objectivity is not universal categoricity; current-preference indifference is not a refutation of Smith’s ideal-corrected agency. Wisdom and veracity remain affirmatively appraised at their separate source-owned scopes.
